headline: Interface-driven tools wrap established engines for RNA, lipid and RNA-seq analysis
label: Open Source Bioinformatics Analysis Tools
summary: Recent preprints and publications describe Galaxy, LLM and web-server wrappers that expose established R, Python and MD engines to users.
synthesis: The dominant thread is delivery of established computational engines through interfaces that lower the barrier to use. R2G2 automatically generates Galaxy XML wrappers for R/Bioconductor packages and manages their dependencies, removing manual wrapper authoring. ARNy Plotter places MDAnalysis, Barnaba and foRNA behind a web server for RMSD, eRMSD, torsion, contact and conformational-landscape analysis of RNA structural ensembles. LNB-MDT couples GUI and script workflows to preparation of lipid nanobubble simulations, trajectory analysis and plotting. REDAC adds a natural-language layer, using LLMs (Gemma, LLaMA) with PubMed retrieval to automate RNA-seq differential expression analysis. What is new across these items is the integration of existing engines into workflow-level interfaces, with REDAC contributing LLM-mediated querying and R2G2 contributing automated wrapper generation. The items share delivery format rather than a single biological target.
